message.content: Elias knows the poison in his tea will kill him within an hour, while Mara knows her execution is scheduled for tomorrow at dawn. Elias drinks the tea calmly to spare her the pain of seeing him suffer a slow death before she must face her own. Mara spends the night arranging their funeral and writing letters, knowing exactly when she must leave this world. Elias realizes that living with the certainty of imminent death makes every passing minute agonizingly precious compared to Mara's single moment of fear. Ultimately, knowing how you will die allows you to accept your end with dignity, whereas knowing only when it comes leaves no time to prepare your soul.
